messages.subject: Linear combinations of predicted responses
parts:
Dear INLA experts,
is it possible to compute linear combinations of predicted responses, e.g. mu=exp(eta), where eta is linear predictor and I would like know variance of sum of some subset of mu?

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear combinations of predicted responses
parts:
On Sat, 2013-07-20 at 22:18 -0700, Jussi wrote:
> Dear INLA experts,
> is it possible to compute linear combinations of predicted responses,
> e.g. mu=exp(eta), where eta is linear predictor and I would like know
> variance of sum of some subset of mu?

no that is not possible. the easiest way out, is use
'inla.posterior.sample', which creates (joint) samples of the eta's, so
you can compute sum exp(eta_i), hence get the variance from there.

if this is not a good option for you, can you can compute the posterior
correlation matrix between linear combinations (eta's in this case), and
then approximate the variance of sum exp(eta_i) using Taylor
expansion.


Best
H
